theory.intro: Every part of a circle has a name. The name depends on whether the part is a straight line, a curve or a region, and on how it meets the **centre** and the **circumference**.
facts: The **centre** is the point that every point on the circle is the same distance from.
The **circumference** is the perimeter of the circle — the distance all the way around it.
A **radius** is a straight line from the centre to the circumference.
A **diameter** is a straight line through the centre joining two points on the circumference, so it is **double** the radius.
A **chord** joins two points on the circumference, and a diameter is the special chord that also passes through the centre.
An **arc** is a part of the circumference.
A **sector** is the region between two radii and an arc.
A **semicircle** is half a circle — a sector whose straight edge is a diameter.
A **quadrant** is a quarter of a circle — a sector whose two radii meet at a right angle.
A chord that misses the centre makes two unequal segments. The smaller is the **minor segment** and the larger is the **major segment**.
steps: Identify the centre, or decide whether the marked part is a straight line, a curve or a region.
For a straight line, check how it meets the centre and the circumference.
For a curve, check whether the whole circumference or only an arc is shown.
For a region, check whether its straight edge is a chord or two radii. Look for a half, a quarter, or the larger or smaller region.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The line joins the centre to the circumference. It is a radius.
(b) The line joins two points on the circumference and passes through the centre. It is a diameter.
(c) The line joins two points on the circumference but misses the centre. It is a chord.
(d) A diameter joins two points on the circumference, so it is a special chord.
(e) The whole curve is the circumference. A part of it is an arc.
(f) It is a tangent.

(a) Two radii and an arc form the boundary. The region is a sector.
(b) A chord and an arc form the boundary, so the region is a segment. It is the larger region made by the chord, so it is the major segment. The smaller unshaded region is the minor segment.

(a) The diameter divides the circle into two equal halves. The shaded half is a semicircle.
(b) The two radii meet at a right angle. The shaded quarter is a quadrant.

foundation.solution_text:
The straight line joins the centre to a point on the circumference.
It is a radius.

The straight line joins two points on the circumference and passes through the centre.
It is a diameter.

The straight line joins two points on the circumference but does not pass through the centre.
It is a chord.

The whole curve around the outside of the circle is highlighted.
It is the circumference.

Only a part of the curve around the outside is highlighted.
It is an arc.

The region is bounded by two radii and an arc.
It is a sector.

The region is bounded by a diameter and an arc, so it is half of the circle.
It is a semicircle.

development.solution_text:
The straight line touches the circumference at exactly one point and does not enter the circle.
It is a tangent.

The region is bounded by a chord and an arc.
It is a segment.

The region is bounded by two radii that meet at a right angle, so it is a quarter of the circle.
It is a quadrant.

Line $1$ joins two points on the circumference, so it is a chord.
Line $3$ joins the centre to the circumference, so it is a radius.
Line $2$ touches the circumference at one point only and does not enter the circle.
Line $2$ is the tangent.

A diameter must pass through the centre, but the red line passes above the centre dot.
It still joins two points on the circumference.
It is a chord.

development.question_text: What name is given to a chord that passes through the centre of a circle?
development.solution_text:
A chord joins two points on the circumference; the one that also passes through the centre is the longest chord of all.
It is a diameter.

development.question_text: What name is given to the region between a chord and the circumference?
development.solution_text:
The region is between a chord and an arc.
It is a segment.

development.question_text: What name is given to the point inside a circle that is the same distance from every point on the circumference?
development.solution_text:
Every radius is drawn from this point, and every radius of a circle is the same length.
It is the centre.

mastery.solution_text:
$1$ joins the centre to the circumference, so it is a radius.
$2$ joins two points on the circumference without passing through the centre, so it is a chord.
$3$ touches the circumference at one point only, so it is a tangent.
$4$ is a part of the circumference, so it is an arc.

$P$ is bounded by two radii and an arc, so it is a sector.
$Q$ is bounded by a chord and an arc, so it is a segment.

mastery.question_text: Explain why every diameter is a chord, but not every chord is a diameter.
mastery.solution_text:
A chord is any straight line joining two points on the circumference.
A diameter joins two points on the circumference as well, so a diameter fits the definition of a chord.
A chord counts as a diameter only when it also passes through the centre, and most chords miss the centre.
